name: Cursor
company: Anysphere (wholly owned subsidiary of SpaceX since Aug 2026)
product: AI-first code editor (VS Code fork) with an autonomous coding agent, tab completion, cloud agents and Bugbot code review.
starting_paid_price: $8/month (Plus, Grok models only, for new customers since Oct 12 2026); Premium $30/month; legacy Pro $20/month for existing subscribers
latest_funding: Acquired by SpaceX in an all-stock deal valued at $60B (announced Jun 16 2026, closed Aug 14 2026); earlier $29.3B post-money valuation
founders_or_ceo: Founded by Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif, Arvid Lunnemark and Aman Sanger (Michael Truell CEO pre-acquisition)
africa_evidence: Cursor's own forum has an Africa events category where Cursor staff post official meetups, including the first official Cursor event and CursorNg community launch in Lagos, Café Cursor Lagos and Nairobi, and a Cursor Kenya meetup featuring Cursor team member Yash Gaitonde.
availability_in_africa: Not found (Cursor docs say some regions only get a subset of models, e.g. Composer, Grok, DeepSeek, Kimi, but no Africa-specific list was found). A discounted 'Start' plan exists only for India.
africa_use_case: Nigerian and Kenyan developers already attending Cursor meetups could fund the $8-$30 plans in naira or shillings via Cozzipay instead of hitting the $20-$100 monthly FX limits on local cards.
notes: Strong grassroots demand in Lagos and Nairobi (official meetups, forum threads asking for emerging-market pricing). Now part of SpaceX, which may slow partnership decisions. New plans are sold through 'The X Subscription' since Oct 2026. A third-party guide notes Nigerian banks cap international card spend at roughly $20-$100/month.

name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
product: Agentic AI IDE (the former Windsurf editor with Cascade agent) renamed Devin Desktop in June 2026, bundled with the Devin autonomous coding agent.
latest_funding: Series E, over $2B at a $48B valuation (2026), led by a16z, Accel, Founders Fund, General Catalyst and Avenir
founders_or_ceo: Scott Wu (CEO), Steven Hao (CTO), Walden Yan (CPO)
africa_use_case: African dev agencies doing outsourced work for foreign clients could pay the $20 Pro plan locally and use Devin agents to take on more contracts.
notes: SWAP NOTE: Windsurf was acquired by Cognition (agreement July 2025) and renamed Devin Desktop on June 2 2026; windsurf.com/pricing redirects to devin.ai/pricing. Kept as the successor product rather than dropped. Teams $80/month base plus $40/seat.

name: GitHub Copilot
product: AI coding assistant and agent across VS Code, JetBrains, the GitHub website, Copilot CLI and the Copilot desktop app.
latest_funding: Part of Microsoft
founders_or_ceo: Not found (GitHub COO Kyle Daigle and CPO Mario Rodriguez appear in recent press)
africa_evidence: GitHub and Microsoft announced a GenAI for Youth programme for young developers in Africa, with GitHub (described as the Copilot-powered developer platform) scaling it with a focus on South Africa, Nigeria and Kenya.
availability_in_africa: Not found (no country restriction found; Copilot Student is free for verified students, and South African guides describe access via paid plan or Student Developer Pack)
payment_methods: Credit card or PayPal (GitHub billing docs)
africa_use_case: African developers who outgrow the free tier or student plan could renew the $10 Pro plan monthly from mobile money without needing a dollar card or PayPal.
notes: Copilot moved to usage-based 'AI Credits' billing on June 1 2026. New Pro, Pro+ and Student sign-ups were temporarily paused from April 20 2026 per a GitHub community thread. Programme evidence links Copilot to Africa only through the GitHub platform description, so it is moderate. Microsoft ownership makes direct partnership harder.

name: Claude Code
product: Agentic coding tool that runs in the terminal, IDEs, desktop and web, included in paid Claude subscriptions.
latest_funding: Not found (press reports Anthropic preparing a public listing at up to $1.4T valuation in late 2026)
founders_or_ceo: Dario Amodei (CEO), co-founded with Daniela Amodei and five others
africa_presence_type: Programme; Partnership (government MoUs at parent level)
africa_evidence: Claude Community Kenya, supported by Anthropic's Claude Community Ambassadors programme, runs Claude Code meetups and Impact Labs in Nairobi; one Impact Lab opened with in-person training by Anthropic's team and gave builders $100 in API credits. Anthropic also signed agreements with Kenya (Sept 2026) and Rwanda (Feb 2026).
availability_in_africa: Anthropic's Supported Regions Policy covers Claude Code and lists many African countries (e.g. Algeria, Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Cote d'Ivoire); a third-party comparison found Ethiopia, Eritrea, Libya, Somalia and Sudan missing from the help-centre version.
payment_methods: Credit and debit cards only for web purchases; ACH for some invoiced Enterprise/API accounts (Anthropic support article)
africa_use_case: Kenyan and Nigerian builders already learning Claude Code at Anthropic-backed events could keep a $20 Pro plan active by paying in local currency, since the web checkout accepts cards only.
notes: Card-only checkout is a clear Cozzipay hook. Large company, but has an active Africa push (Kenya, Rwanda, TCS partnership for South Africa). Usage pool shared with claude.ai and Cowork. Max $100, Ultra $200.

name: OpenAI Codex
product: Coding agent (CLI, IDE extension, desktop app and cloud tasks) included in ChatGPT plans.
latest_funding: Not found
africa_evidence: OpenAI's multi-currency billing page lists NGN (Nigeria), ZAR (South Africa), EGP (Egypt) and TZS (Tanzania) for ChatGPT web subscriptions, which include Codex. OpenAI and Andela also run a pan-African Codex Champions Series, including a Lagos showcase in Oct 2026.
availability_in_africa: ChatGPT Go launched in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Egypt and Morocco; OpenAI publishes a supported-countries list. OpenAI Academy launched in Lagos with an Africa Lead.
payment_methods: Not found (multi-currency web billing; app-store billing in local currency on iOS/Android)
africa_use_case: Developers in African countries not on OpenAI's local-currency list (e.g. Kenya, Ghana) could pay ChatGPT Plus for Codex from mobile money.
notes: Already prices in naira and rand, so the pitch should focus on countries without local billing and on users without cards. Large company with an Africa lead (Emmanuel Lubanzadio) who could be a contact point.

name: Google Antigravity
product: Agent-first development platform (desktop app and CLI) where AI agents plan, write, run and test code.
starting_paid_price: $19.99/month via Google AI Pro (NGN 28,500/month in Nigeria)
latest_funding: Part of Google (Alphabet)
africa_evidence: Google's Nigerian subscriptions page prices Google AI Pro at NGN 28,500/month and Ultra from NGN 89,000/month, and lists Antigravity agent rate limits as a benefit of those plans. Google also offered its top AI plan free for a year to university students in Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa and Zimbabwe.
availability_in_africa: Google AI Pro is listed as available in more than 150 countries; Nigerian pricing page exists. GDG chapters in Kenya and Nigeria run community Antigravity workshops.
africa_use_case: Ghanaian or Kenyan developers whose cards fail on Google Play could top up Google AI Pro for higher Antigravity limits through Cozzipay.
notes: SWAP NOTE: replaces Gemini Code Assist, which Google is winding down (individual free tier stopped June 18 2026; no new Standard/Enterprise subscriptions from Oct 9 2026) and which points users to Antigravity. Paid capacity is sold through Google AI plans, not a standalone Antigravity plan. Hard for a payments startup to reach Google.

name: Kiro
product: Spec-driven agentic AI IDE and CLI that turns prompts into requirements, designs, task lists and code; successor to Amazon Q Developer.
latest_funding: Part of Amazon
africa_evidence: Only community activity found: the AWS AI/ML User Group Kenya ran 'Kiro Nights Nairobi' buildathons. AWS itself has African programmes (re/Start, a Vodacom AI for Africa hackathon) but no source ties them to Kiro.
payment_methods: Card (Kiro blog describes charging the subscriber's card)
africa_use_case: AWS-focused developers in Nairobi and Lagos could keep Kiro Pro credits topped up from local bank transfer instead of a dollar card.
notes: Self-serve plans: Pro $20, Pro+ $40, Pro Max $100, Power $200; extra credits $0.04. AWS ownership makes direct partnership harder, but community user groups in Kenya are active.

name: Warp
product: Open-source agentic development environment built from the terminal, with built-in coding agents, a CLI agent and the Oz cloud-agent platform.
latest_funding: Series B, $50M led by Sequoia (June 2023); about $73M raised in total
africa_use_case: Backend and DevOps engineers in Lagos or Cape Town could subscribe to the $20 Build plan and reload agent credits from mobile money.
notes: SWAP NOTE: replaces Amazon Q Developer, which closed to new sign-ups on May 15 2026 and loses support on April 30 2027 in favour of Kiro. Warp also publishes press@warp.dev and billing@warp.dev. Mid-size startup with self-serve credit reloads, a good fit for prepaid wallet top-ups.

name: JetBrains AI (AI Assistant and Junie)
product: AI Assistant chat and completion plus the Junie coding agent inside JetBrains IDEs and a CLI, sold as AI credit tiers.
latest_funding: Not found (privately held, no outside funding found)
africa_evidence: No African office, local pricing or partner found. Purchase terms route South African customers to JetBrains Distributions s.r.o. in Prague, which is a Czech entity, not an African one.
availability_in_africa: JetBrains AI service territory list includes African countries such as Nigeria, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Niger, Rwanda, Senegal, Malawi, Mali, Mauritius, Madagascar and Sierra Leone.
payment_methods: Credit or debit card, PayPal, or other instant regional methods online; organisations can also use wire transfer or purchase orders
africa_use_case: African Kotlin, Java and Android developers who already use IntelliJ could add AI Pro or AI Ultimate credits paid in local currency.
notes: JetBrains runs a reseller programme; no African reseller was found in searches. AI Ultimate $30/month. AI tiers are often bundled with IDE subscriptions.

name: Tabnine
product: Privacy-focused enterprise AI coding platform with completions, chat, agents, CLI and on-prem or air-gapped deployment.
latest_funding: Acquired by Tricentis, July 30 2026 (price reported at tens of millions of dollars)
africa_use_case: Regulated African banks and telcos that cannot send code to public clouds could use Tabnine's self-hosted option, but they would buy through enterprise invoicing.
notes: Kept because the product still exists, but after the Tricentis acquisition the old pricing page redirects to a Tricentis contact form. No individual plan; enterprise sales only, so little card dependency.

name: Amp
product: Frontier multi-model coding agent for terminal and editors, with hosted cloud machines ('orbs') per thread.
starting_paid_price: $20/month (Megawatt individual plan; $10/month for students and teachers)
latest_funding: Not found (spun out of Sourcegraph as an independent company in December 2025)
africa_use_case: African university students could take the $10 student Megawatt plan and pay it from a Cozzipay wallet funded by mobile money.
notes: Sourcegraph (code search) and Amp became separate companies; Dan Adler leads Sourcegraph. Amp Free admission closed Feb 2026, then switched to a daily free-credit grant. Small team (about 21 people per an Oct 2026 profile).

name: OpenCode
product: MIT-licensed, provider-agnostic AI coding agent for terminal, desktop and IDEs, with optional paid Go and Zen model plans.
latest_funding: Not found
founders_or_ceo: Not found (built by the team behind SST and terminal.shop)
africa_use_case: Budget-conscious African developers could pay the $10 Go plan for flat-rate open-model coding without a dollar card.
notes: SWAP NOTE: replaces Continue, which was acquired by Cursor in 2026 (continue.dev now says so). Low price point and huge open-source user base suit Cozzipay. Go Plus $40/month, Go Teams $20/member. Email published by maintainers in GitHub issues for billing support.

name: Cline
product: Open-source autonomous coding agent for VS Code and other editors, plus CLI, desktop beta and cloud sessions, with bring-your-own-key or Cline credits.
latest_funding: Seed and Series A, $32M combined, led by Emergence Capital and Pace Capital (July 2025)
africa_use_case: Solo developers in Africa could top up Cline credits in small amounts from a mobile-money-funded wallet as they use them.
notes: Over 11 million installs (Oct 2026). Users wanting to avoid Cline credits can bring their own API key, which shifts payment to model providers. Also publishes support@cline.bot for billing.

name: Factory (Droid)
product: Multi-model software development agents ('Droids') for terminal, IDE and enterprise workflows.
latest_funding: $200M at a $5B valuation (2026), after a $150M Series C at $1.5B led by Khosla Ventures (April 2026)
africa_use_case: African fintech engineering teams could run Droids on a self-serve plan paid from a business Cozzipay wallet.
notes: SWAP NOTE: replaces Roo Code, which shut down its VS Code extension, cloud and router on May 15 2026 and archived the repo. Factory is more enterprise-oriented; confirm self-serve pricing on factory.ai/pricing.

name: Kilo Code
product: Open-source coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains, CLI and desktop with a 500+ model gateway at provider rates.
latest_funding: Acquired by Anaconda, July 2026; earlier $8M seed led by Cota Capital (Dec 2025)
founders_or_ceo: Scott Breitenother (co-founder and CEO), with Sid Sijbrandij (GitLab co-founder)
africa_use_case: Kilo Pass converts payments 1:1 into credits, so African developers could buy prepaid credit packs in local currency through Cozzipay.
notes: Kept because products, plans and support continued unchanged after the Anaconda deal. Kilo runs partner hackathons, which could be a co-marketing angle for an African hackathon.

name: Augment Code
product: AI coding agent and IDE extensions built around a Context Engine that indexes large codebases, plus the Auggie CLI and Intent.
latest_funding: Series B, $227M (April 2024), $252M total
founders_or_ceo: Founded by Igor Ostrovsky and Guy Gur-Ari; CEO reported as Matt McClernan by Oct 2025 (Scott Dietzen led at launch)
africa_use_case: Engineers maintaining large codebases at African banks or telcos could buy the $20 Indie plan without a corporate dollar card.
notes: Pricing changed several times; Standard $60 and Max $200 per developer on the credit model. Mostly enterprise-focused.

name: Zed
product: Fast open-source Rust code editor with built-in AI agent, edit predictions and support for external agents.
latest_funding: Series B, $32M led by Sequoia Capital (Aug 2025), over $42M total
founders_or_ceo: Nathan Sobo (co-founder), with Antonio Scandurra and Max Brunsfeld
africa_use_case: Developers on modest laptops in Africa who prefer a lightweight editor could pay the $10 Pro plan monthly from mobile money.
notes: Low price, small reachable team, and a published contact address. Business plan $30/seat/month.

name: TRAE
product: AI-native IDE with an autonomous SOLO agent mode, IDE mode and a broader Work mode.
latest_funding: Part of ByteDance
africa_evidence: TRAE Friends @ Nigeria was a virtual meetup for Nigerian developers co-hosted by Tennxt and the TRAE Community, demonstrating TRAE SOLO and MCP links to payment gateways.
africa_use_case: TRAE's $3 Lite plan is cheap enough for African students and beginners, if they can pay it without an international card.
notes: Evidence is a single virtual community event, so the 'In Africa' label is borderline. Third-party sources disagree on prices (Pro listed at $10 and $20); confirm on trae.ai/pricing. ByteDance ownership may complicate partnership.

name: Qoder
product: Agentic coding platform (desktop IDE, JetBrains plugin, CLI and mobile) with Repo Wiki and multi-agent Experts Mode.
latest_funding: Part of Alibaba
africa_use_case: African developers could buy the $10 Lite plan or $20 credit packs through Cozzipay, which fits prepaid wallet top-ups.
notes: Plans: Lite $10, Pro $20, Pro+ $60, Ultra $200; credit packs $20 per 1,500 credits, non-refundable. A separate Qoder CN product serves China.

name: Mistral Vibe
product: Mistral's unified agent (formerly Le Chat) that includes a coding agent for CLI, VS Code and remote sandboxes.
latest_funding: Not found
africa_evidence: Mistral AI has a partnership with Morocco's digital ministry, with reports of Morocco becoming its regional AI hub and joint Darija tools, but no source links it to Vibe or its coding agent.
africa_use_case: Francophone developers in Morocco, Senegal and Cote d'Ivoire could pay Vibe Pro in local currency; Mistral's Morocco ties make it a natural North/West Africa pitch.
notes: SWAP NOTE: replaces Void, which was deprecated and its GitHub repo archived on June 2 2026. Le Chat was renamed Vibe in June 2026. Team $24.99/user/month; student price reported at $5.99.

name: Tabby
product: Open-source, self-hosted AI coding assistant with completions, chat, repository context and an agent, running on your own GPU.
latest_funding: Not found
africa_use_case: African teams with patchy connectivity or data-residency needs could self-host Tabby and pay Team seats through a Cozzipay business wallet.
notes: Free Community edition for up to 5 users; most users self-host for free, so paid volume is small.

name: Aider
product: Open-source terminal AI pair programmer that edits files in a local git repo and auto-commits changes, using your own model API keys.
starting_paid_price: Not found (free and open source; users pay model providers)
latest_funding: Not found
africa_use_case: Aider has nothing to sell, but African Aider users still need to pay model APIs, so Cozzipay's pitch belongs with those providers.
notes: No paid plan, so there is no merchant checkout to integrate. Useful only as a channel or community partner.

name: Pieces
product: On-device AI developer assistant with long-term memory of workflow context across IDEs, browsers and tools, plus an MCP server for coding agents.
latest_funding: Series A, $13.5M led by Drive Capital (July 2024)
africa_use_case: African freelancers working across many client projects could pay for Pieces Pro memory in local currency.
notes: Coding-adjacent (memory and context layer rather than an editor). Based in Cincinnati, Ohio. Annual plan $169.99.

name: CodeGPT
product: AI coding assistant and agent platform for VS Code and JetBrains with bring-your-own-key, local models and paid model access.
starting_paid_price: About $10/month (Professional, per third-party reviews; an official docs page shows an $8/month plan)
latest_funding: Not found
founders_or_ceo: Daniel Avila Arias and Alvaro Chavez (founders)
africa_use_case: African students and junior developers could keep a cheap CodeGPT plan renewing monthly from a mobile-money-funded wallet.
notes: Miami-based startup founded in 2023, over 2.4 million VS Code installs. Several unrelated tools use the 'CodeGPT' name; confirm the correct company before outreach. Price sources disagree ($8-$10).
